body.x: SEOUL, Korea (AVING Special Report on 'WIS 2008') -- <Visual News> Samsung and LG Electronics expect to release its MIDs for an Internet experience in your pocket in the second half of the year.

In 2006, Samsung had joined forces with Intel to present the world's first UMPC, while getting less than they expected. Now Samsung chose Snapdragon platform form Qualcomm. According to an official of Qualcomm, Snapdragon-powered MID from Samsung is expected to hit retail stores in the end of June, 2008.

Running on 1GHz ARMv7 microprocessor, the Samsung MID will offer unsurpassed mobile performance and power savings. At the core of Snapdragon is the Scorpion which is paired with a 128 bit single-instruction, multiple-data capability and Qualcomm's next-generation 600 MHz digital signal processor.

Supporting 12M built-in camera, GPS and HD video playback, the Samsung MID will also deliver a broad array of mobile broadband capabilities, including CDMA2000/EV-DO, WCDMA(UMTS)/HSDPA/HSUPA, broadcast television and multimedia, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
(Picture: Qualcomm to unveil the display equipped with Snapdragon during World IT Show)
On the other side, LG goes with Intel's Menlow platform. LG is going to launch its Menlow-based MID in global market, according to the company.

The Intel Atom processor is based on an entirely new microarchitecture designed specifically for small devices and low power, while maintaining the Intel Core 2 Duo instruction set compatibility consumers are accustomed to when using a standard PC and the Internet. These new chips are manufactured on Intel's industry-leading 45nm process with hi-k metal gate technology. The chips have a thermal design power(TDP) specification in 0.6-2.5 watt range and scale to 1.8GHz speeds depending on customer need.

(Picture: LG Electronics presented its 4.8-inch MID prototype during CES 2008, which is based on Intel's Menlow platform and Silverthorn CPU. Adopting a sliding touch screen and qwerty keyboard, it is equipped with 1GB DDR2 memory and 40GB hard drive. It also supports HSDPA, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity)
